cards.explanation: The answer is wise. Jesus says five were foolish and five were wise (Matthew 25:2). Ten lamps, ten virgins, and two very different kinds of planning. You can see the split in the next verses: the foolish ones did not take along any extra oil, but the wise ones took oil in flasks along with their lamps.

The answer is extra oil. The foolish ones took their lamps but did not take along any extra oil (Matthew 25:3). That's like me starting a batch with exactly enough dough and nothing set aside for the next tray. It all works fine, right up until you need more.

The answer is False. The text says that when the bridegroom was delayed, “…they all became drowsy and fell asleep.” (Matthew 25:5) That means all ten, the wise ones too. Sleeping wasn't the difference between them, friends, and I think that's kind of comforting.

The answer is False. The text says, “Then all the virgins woke up and trimmed their lamps.” (Matthew 25:7) The foolish ones heard the cry like everybody else. Nobody slept through it, so the real problem is coming in the next verse.

The answer is that their lamps are going out. The foolish ones tell the wise, “Give us some of your oil; our lamps are going out.” (Matthew 25:8) I'd say that's a stressful sentence to say out loud at midnight. They took those lamps along to go out and meet the bridegroom (Matthew 25:1), and now the lamps are going out.

The answer is False. The wise ones answer, “No,” saying there may not be enough for both them and the foolish ones (Matthew 25:9). It's a tough moment, and I think it catches a lot of bakers off guard. They send the foolish five to someone else for oil.

The answer is that there may not be enough for both. The wise ones say, “or there may not be enough for both us and you.” (Matthew 25:9) That's the reason they give, and it's the only one the text gives. Oil only stretches so far.

The answer is True. The wise ones say, “Instead, go to those who sell oil and buy some for yourselves.” (Matthew 25:9) It's an actual plan, not a slammed door. I just think midnight is a rough hour to go shopping.

The answer is False. The text says, “But while they were on their way to buy it, the bridegroom arrived.” (Matthew 25:10) So he arrives while the foolish five are away, and the ones who were ready go in with him. The foolish five weren't there yet. The timing is the whole story, friends.

The answer is shut. The ones who were ready went in with the bridegroom to the wedding banquet, “…and the door was shut.” (Matthew 25:10) A few small words, and a lot of weight. I think this is the moment the story turns.

The answer is I do not know you. The bridegroom replies, “Truly I tell you, I do not know you.” (Matthew 25:12) I think this one hurts, friends. It's the heaviest line in the whole story, so we'll let it sit for a second.

The answer is that you do not know the day or the hour. Jesus says, “Therefore keep watch, because you do not know the day or the hour.” (Matthew 25:13) Earlier, Jesus says only the Father knows that day (Matthew 24:36). That's why my ovens stay warm and ready, friends. I'm not guessing at a date, I'm just keeping the oven on.
